title: Kanban: flow, work-in-progress limits and continuous quality

videos.script: Célia asked for a change to the price sign. It took Rafael one afternoon. She saw it three weeks later. {{sign}} Where did the other days go? Nobody was idle. Everybody was busy. {{busy}} So Lia drew the work on a board, a column for each step, and a column for waiting. {{board}} That column told the story. Cards sat in waiting for test for five days, and testing itself took one. {{wait}} Kanban's answer is a limit. When a column is full, nobody starts anything new. You help the card in front of you move instead. Stop starting, start finishing. {{limit}} Fewer cards on the board, the same people, the same speed, and every card comes out sooner. That is Little's law, and it is arithmetic. {{law}} Then the rules for leaving each column, written at the top of it, so quality is built in at every step, not checked at the end. {{end}}
